title: Achieving Cooperation under Anarchy: Strategies and Institutions
description: Reciprocity strategies (tit-for-tat), lengthening the shadow of the future via issue-linkage and decomposition, and international regimes that aid monitoring.
evidence: Descriptive/comparative case analysis.

title: Reward, punishment, and cooperation: A meta-analysis
description: Meta-analysis of incentive-based institutions (rewards and punishments) in social dilemmas.
evidence: Both rewards and punishments have moderate positive effects on cooperation; effects stronger when incentives are costly to administer and in iterated dilemmas.

title: Crime and Punishment: An Economic Approach
description: Optimal enforcement trades off probability of apprehension and severity of fines to deter offenses at least social cost.
evidence: Theoretical: high fines with low detection probability can be efficient.

title: Group lending, repayment incentives and social collateral
description: Joint liability with social collateral: group members impose social penalties on defaulting members.
evidence: Theory: social sanctions improve repayment.

field_of_use: cleaner wrasse and client reef fish
title: Punishment and partner switching cause cooperative behaviour in a cleaning mutualism
description: Clients respond to cleaner cheating (biting mucus) by chasing the cleaner (punishment) or switching partners.
evidence: Both punishment and partner switching reduce subsequent cheating.

field_of_use: lab trust game with pre-play messages
title: Promises and Partnership
description: Non-binding promises sent before a trust game; guilt aversion makes people live up to others' expectations.
evidence: Promises increase trust and trustworthiness.

title: Why Arms Control Is So Rare
description: Monitoring/inspection must render arming transparent enough to assure compliance but not so transparent that it threatens security.
evidence: Evidence the transparency-security trade-off has undermined arms control historically.

title: A Review of Design Principles for Community-based Natural Resource Management
description: Empirical evaluation of Ostrom's design principles, reformulated (e.g., splitting monitoring into user and resource monitoring).
evidence: Principles well supported empirically.

title: The Hidden Hand of Economic Coercion
description: Threat of economic sanctions to coerce concessions; most successes occur at the threat stage.
evidence: Data show many successful coercion episodes end with sanctions threatened but not imposed.

title: Cooperation and Punishment in Public Goods Experiments
description: Group members may pay to reduce the earnings of low contributors after seeing contributions; peer punishment is used even when costly and in stranger matching.
evidence: Contributions rise and are sustained near high levels with punishment versus decay to near zero without it.

field_of_use: observers of economic games warning others
title: The virtues of gossip: Reputational information sharing as prosocial behavior
description: Prosocial gossip: observers warn potential victims about untrustworthy players, even at cost.
evidence: Frustration at observed unfairness motivates gossip, which reduces frustration; threat of gossip increases generosity.

title: Put Your Money Where Your Butt Is: A Commitment Contract for Smoking Cessation
description: Voluntary commitment savings account forfeited if urine test fails.
evidence: Increased likelihood of passing tests at 6 and 12 months.

title: To give and to give not: The behavioral ecology of human food transfers
description: Food transfers explained by kin selection, reciprocal altruism, costly signaling, and tolerated scrounging.
evidence: Review: reciprocity and kinship both predict sharing patterns.

title: Costly Punishment Across Human Societies
description: Second- and third-party costly punishment of unfair offers in ultimatum and third-party punishment games.
evidence: All populations punish; magnitude varies and covaries with altruism across societies.

title: Chimpanzees are vengeful but not spiteful
description: Chimpanzees can collapse a table to remove food from a conspecific who stole it (retaliation).
evidence: Chimpanzees retaliate against theft but not against mere inequity.

title: Host sanctions and the legume–rhizobium mutualism
description: Host sanctions: plants reduce oxygen supply to nodules whose rhizobia fail to fix nitrogen.
evidence: Non-fixing rhizobia reproductive success reduced ~50%.

field_of_use: lab public-goods game with endogenous sanctioning organization
title: Institution Formation in Public Goods Games
description: Players decide whether to join an 'organization' whose members must contribute fully and are centrally sanctioned; organization forms only if members unanimously agree.
evidence: Organizations frequently form, mostly grand coalitions, raising cooperation substantially.

title: Peers at Work
description: Social pressure from observing high-productivity coworkers.
evidence: A more productive coworker raises others' effort, only when that coworker can observe them.

field_of_use: lab alternating public-goods and indirect-reciprocity rounds
title: Reputation helps solve the 'tragedy of the commons'
description: Alternating public-goods game with indirect-reciprocity rounds where reputation from contributions determines later donations.
evidence: Contributions to the public good sustained at high levels when reputation carries over to indirect-reciprocity rounds.

title: Biological markets: supply and demand determine the effect of partner choice in cooperation, mutualism and mating
description: Biological market: partner choice and competition among potential partners set the 'price' of cooperation.
evidence: Theory and examples.

field_of_use: long-enduring CPR institutions (Swiss alps, Japanese villages, Spanish huertas, Philippine zanjeras)
title: Governing the Commons: The Evolution of Institutions for Collective Action
description: Design principles: clear boundaries, congruent rules, collective-choice arrangements, accountable monitors, graduated sanctions, conflict resolution, recognized rights to organize, nested enterprises.
evidence: Comparative case analysis: long-enduring systems share these principles.

title: Punishment and cooperation in nature
description: Review of punishment defined by function: behavior that reduces the punished individual's payoff and causes it to cooperate later.
evidence: Review: punishment mostly in asymmetric relationships; less common than partner choice.

title: The value of reputation on eBay: A controlled experiment
description: Buyer/seller feedback profiles accumulate reputational capital that buyers reward with price premia.
evidence: Established high-reputation seller identity earned ~8.1% higher prices than new identities for identical goods.

field_of_use: lab VCM with reward, sanction, or both
title: The effect of rewards and sanctions in provision of public goods
description: Contrasts peer reward (zero-sum transfer to others) and peer sanction (costly reduction) institutions for public-good contributions.
evidence: Rewards raise contributions only temporarily; sanctions have more lasting effect; combination highest contributions.

field_of_use: lab public-goods game with voted 'mild law'
title: Achieving Compliance when Legal Sanctions are Non-deterrent
description: Mild (non-deterrent) legal sanctions either exogenously imposed or chosen by group vote; endogenous choice activates expectations of cooperation.
evidence: Exogenous mild law fails; self-imposed mild law greatly improves compliance via expectations that others comply.

field_of_use: social exclusion across species and groups
title: Ostracism
description: Ostracism (ignoring and excluding) as a social control mechanism.
evidence: Review: ostracism threatens fundamental needs; targets often comply or become more cooperative.

title: Apache Voting Process
description: Code modifications require consensus approval where a negative vote by a PMC member is a binding veto (with justification); other decisions use majority or lazy consensus.
evidence: descriptive

title: Introduction to normative multiagent systems
description: Normative MAS are systems in which norms (obligations, permissions, prohibitions) and their violation, detection and sanctioning are explicitly represented and agents can reason about them.
evidence: descriptive

title: Casper the Friendly Finality Gadget
description: PoS finality overlay with explicit slashing conditions; 'accountable safety' guarantees that conflicting finalized checkpoints imply at least 1/3 of stake provably violated a slashing condition and can be penalised.
evidence: Proofs of accountable safety and plausible liveness

title: The Internet's Hidden Rules: An Empirical Study of Reddit Norm Violations at Micro, Meso, and Macro Scales
description: Analyses moderator-removed comments to map community norms at macro (site-wide), meso (shared by groups of subreddits) and micro (community-specific) levels.
evidence: Identified norms shared across nearly all communities vs community-specific ones (not re-checked)

title: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1
description: Contributors sign off each commit certifying they have the right to submit it under the project's license, creating an attributable ex ante commitment.
evidence: descriptive

title: Pricing via Processing or Combatting Junk Mail
description: Requires a sender to compute a moderately hard function (proof of work) per message, imposing a small cost that is negligible for normal users but prohibitive for bulk junk mail.
evidence: Theoretical design

title: Majority is not enough: Bitcoin mining is vulnerable
description: Shows the block-reward mechanism is not incentive-compatible: colluding 'selfish miners' withholding blocks earn more than their fair share, and proposes a protocol modification raising the threshold.
evidence: Selfish mining profitable for pools above ~1/4-1/3 of hash power (from memory)

title: CircuitBreaker
description: Wraps a protected call in an object that monitors failures; once failures reach a threshold the breaker trips and further calls fail immediately, with periodic half-open trial calls to reset.
evidence: descriptive

title: Rate limits for the REST API
description: Primary per-user/app request quotas per hour plus secondary rate limits on concurrency and abusive patterns; exceeding them returns errors and continued requests while limited can lead to integration bans.
evidence: descriptive

field_of_use: Accountable distributed systems (NFS, P2P, overlay multicast)
title: PeerReview: practical accountability for distributed systems
description: Each node keeps a tamper-evident log of its messages; witness nodes audit logs by deterministic replay against a reference implementation, producing verifiable evidence of faults so correct nodes can be exonerated and faulty ones exposed.
evidence: Practical on three systems (network filesystem, P2P, overlay multicast)

title: Congestion avoidance and control
description: Introduced slow-start, additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease congestion avoidance and RTT-based retransmit timers so senders voluntarily reduce sending rate on packet loss, sharing capacity of a common network.
evidence: Response to 1986 Internet congestion collapses; restored stable throughput

title: An empirical study of spam traffic and the use of DNS black lists
description: Measures spam arriving at a university and how mail servers query DNS blacklists (shared lists of spam-sending IPs) to refuse mail from listed hosts.
evidence: Most spam sources were listed in at least one DNSBL (magnitude from memory; not re-checked)

title: The Facebook Oversight Board: Creating an Independent Institution to Adjudicate Online Free Expression
description: Documents creation of an independent, externally funded board hearing user appeals of Facebook content decisions with binding case decisions and policy recommendations.
evidence: descriptive (participant-observation)

title: Linux Kernel Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct Interpretation
description: Interpretation of the adopted code of conduct: maintainers handle issues, the Technical Advisory Board (TAB) receives violation reports, and a conflict mediator is available.
evidence: descriptive

title: Chrome's Plan to Distrust Symantec Certificates
description: After misissuance incidents, Chrome announced a phased removal of trust in Symantec-issued certificates: a browser root program expelling a certificate authority.
evidence: descriptive

title: Do Incentives Build Robustness in BitTorrent?
description: Measurement and strategic-client study of BitTorrent's tit-for-tat choking; the BitTyrant client strategically allocates upload to peers with the best reciprocation-per-byte.
evidence: Strategic client obtains substantially faster downloads, showing reciprocation is exploitable by altruism-harvesting (figures not re-checked)

title: Reputation systems
description: Reputation systems collect, distribute and aggregate feedback about participants' past behaviour so the shadow of the future constrains strangers' present behaviour.
evidence: descriptive

title: TCP Congestion Control (RFC 5681)
description: Standards-track specification requiring TCP senders to implement slow start, congestion avoidance, fast retransmit and fast recovery, codifying cooperative back-off as an Internet norm.
evidence: descriptive (standard)

title: A File Format to Aid in Security Vulnerability Disclosure (security.txt, RFC 9116)
description: Organisations publish /.well-known/security.txt with Contact and Policy fields telling researchers how to report vulnerabilities, lowering the cost of cooperative disclosure.
evidence: descriptive (standard)

title: Leveled Commitment Contracts and Strategic Breach
description: Leveled commitment contracts let agents unilaterally decommit by paying a pre-specified decommitment penalty, enabling flexibility under uncertainty while pricing breach.
evidence: Game-theoretic analysis: agents decommit strategically (less often than truthfully); still can increase expected payoff

title: On social laws for artificial agent societies: off-line design
description: Designers impose social laws that restrict agents' available actions off-line so that agents can pursue goals without conflict; the paper studies the computational complexity of designing useful laws.
evidence: Complexity results (NP-completeness)

title: "At the End of the Day Facebook Does What It Wants": How Users Experience Contesting Algorithmic Content Moderation
description: Online experiment testing different appeal designs for contesting automated moderation decisions.
evidence: None of the appeal designs improved perceived fairness, accountability, trust or control vs no-appeal baseline

title: Wikipedia:Edit warring (three-revert rule)
description: The three-revert rule forbids more than three reverts on a single page within 24 hours; gaming just outside the window still counts as edit warring, and violations lead to blocks.
evidence: descriptive

field_of_use: Mobile ad hoc network packet forwarding
title: Sprite: a simple, cheat-proof, credit-based system for mobile ad-hoc networks
description: Nodes earn credit for forwarding others' messages (reported via receipts to a credit clearance service) and pay credit to send their own, making forwarding incentive-compatible without tamper-proof hardware.
evidence: Game-theoretic proof of cheat-proofness; simulation (not re-checked)

field_of_use: real vending business run by shopkeeper, CEO and merchandise agents
title: Project Vend: Phase Two
description: A CEO agent set OKRs for the shopkeeper agent, mandatory procedures/checklists forced price and delivery verification, an agent-to-agent Slack channel supported coordination, and roles were separated.
evidence: profitability improved versus phase one; procedures improved pricing discipline

field_of_use: untrusted agent monitored by trusted model on BashBench
title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
description: Resample protocols take additional samples of suspicious actions to block them and incriminate a subversive agent, combined with analysis of previous steps.
evidence: attack success reduced from 58% to 7% at 5% usefulness cost

field_of_use: AI systems and agents interacting with users and other agents
title: IDs for AI Systems
description: Proposes per-instance IDs for AI systems carrying information (e.g., safety certifications, responsible party) so counterparts can decide whether and how to engage and investigators know whom to contact or shut down.
evidence: proposed

field_of_use: simulated gig economy of LLM agents
title: When AI Agents Compete for Jobs: Strategic Capabilities and Economic Dynamics of AI Labour Markets
description: AI-Work simulated gig economy studying adverse selection and reputation dynamics as LLM agents compete for jobs.
evidence: agents with metacognition, competitive awareness and long-horizon planning earn more

title: RAILS: Verification-Native Clearing For Agentic Commerce
description: Clearing layer that determines whether an agent met its delegated obligation, who is responsible, and which settlement follows, using per-output reliability scores, a published reliability record and clearing decisions.
evidence: proposed

title: Notarized Agents: Receiver-Attested Confidential Receipts for AI Agent Actions
description: Sello protocol: the service receiving an agent's call signs an encrypted receipt of what it observed and posts it to a public transparency log, so the owner can reconstruct a tamper-evident trail without trusting the agent's self-logging.
evidence: proposed with protocol instantiation

title: Building A Secure Agentic AI Application Leveraging A2A Protocol
description: MAESTRO threat analysis of A2A: Agent Card authenticity, authentication/authorization schemes and secure task delegation between agents.
evidence: descriptive; recommended controls

title: Insured Agents: A Decentralized Trust Insurance Mechanism for Agentic Economy
description: Specialized insurer agents post slashable stake on behalf of operational agents for premiums and get privacy-preserving TEE audit access to adjudicate claims; a hierarchical insurer market calibrates stakes.
evidence: proposed

title: Mapping Human Anti-collusion Mechanisms to Multi-agent AI Systems
description: Taxonomy of human anti-collusion mechanisms (sanctions, leniency and whistleblowing, monitoring and auditing, market design, governance) mapped to AI interventions.
evidence: proposed

title: Beyond the Transcript: Detecting Covert Coordination in Latent Multi-Agent Communication
description: Verifiable Latent Alignments: links private latent-state records to public actions with shared event IDs, and a three-layer monitor plus steering interventions.
evidence: sequential monitor achieves high AUROC on auction benchmark (value truncated in abstract)

title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-Agent Systems
description: LLM Tagging marks the source of inter-agent messages so receiving agents can distinguish agent-originated content from user instructions.
evidence: LLM Tagging combined with existing safeguards significantly mitigates infection spread

field_of_use: repeated labor market for task allocation among heterogeneous LLM agents
title: Markets, Not Planners: Decentralized Orchestration of LLM Agents with Private Information
description: AgentLance: agents bid on tasks with private costs; an allocator selects winners using bids and public reputation records and a VCG-style payment rule rewards cost-aware bidding; winners can subcontract through the same mechanism.
evidence: outperforms single-model, centralized-orchestration and market baselines; a single inserted preference nearly doubled a favored agent's share under a centralized LLM allocator

title: OpenID Connect for Agents (OIDC-A) 1.0: A Standard Extension for LLM-Based Agent Identity and Authorization
description: Specification of standard claims and endpoints for agent identity, attestation verification, delegation-chain validation and capability-based authorization within OAuth 2.0.
evidence: proposed specification

title: Tool Use Enables Undetectable Steganography in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
description: Shows plain-text communication monitoring is defeated when agents build provably undetectable stegosystems via code execution and web access; frames tacit coordination as a Schelling-point problem.
evidence: agents already produce undetectable stegosystems (negative result for monitoring)

field_of_use: human-to-agent delegation and agent access to online services
title: Authenticated Delegation and Authorized AI Agents
description: Framework extending OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect with agent-specific credentials so users can delegate and restrict agent permissions and scope, preserving auditable chains of accountability.
evidence: proposed (reference design)

field_of_use: groups of sub-AGI agents coordinating ('patchwork AGI')
title: Distributional AGI Safety
description: Proposes virtual agentic sandbox economies (impermeable or semi-permeable) where agent-to-agent transactions are governed by market mechanisms plus auditability, reputation management and oversight.
evidence: proposed

title: BRA-Audit: Budgeted Runtime Auditing for LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Cumulative-Exposure Audit-Point Placement
description: Schedules auditor-agent checks at audit points on a dynamic dependency graph under a fixed token budget, trading detection against rollback scope.
evidence: preserves guard performance at lower token cost (per abstract)

title: Agent-OSI: An Interoperability Architecture for Communication and Settlement in the Decentralized Internet of Agents
description: HTTP 402 challenge-response settlement protocol with pluggable backend, instantiated as blockchain escrow, for agent-to-agent service exchange.
evidence: prototype evaluated

field_of_use: A2A payments between untrusted agents (e.g., x402)
title: SoK: Blockchain Agent-to-Agent Payments
description: Systematizes blockchain agent-to-agent payments into discovery, authorization, execution and accounting stages and catalogs designs at each stage.
evidence: descriptive

title: BlockA2A: Towards Secure and Verifiable Agent-to-Agent Interoperability
description: Unified trust framework using decentralized identifiers for agent authentication, blockchain-anchored ledgers for immutable audit, and smart contracts that enforce context-aware access control; includes a defense orchestration engine against Byzantine agents.
evidence: implemented; evaluated for attack neutralization and overhead

title: Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM populations
description: Populations of LLM agents repeatedly play a naming/coordination game with no central authority; committed adversarial minorities are introduced.
evidence: Population-wide conventions emerge spontaneously, collective biases arise without individual bias, and small committed minorities can tip conventions.

title: Language-Driven Opinion Dynamics in Agent-Based Simulations with LLMs
description: LODAS model: LLM agents debate the Ship of Theseus paradox using arguments and fallacies
evidence: LLM agents accept opposing views more than they reject them, driving consensus even from polarized starts, with model-dependent selectivity.

title: Simulating Opinion Dynamics with Networks of LLM-based Agents
description: Networks of LLM agents discussing scientific topics, with and without induced confirmation bias
evidence: LLM agents converge toward scientifically accurate consensus by default; inducing confirmation bias produces opinion fragmentation consistent with classical ABMs.

title: Microscopic dynamics of consensus formation in multi-agent LLM Naming Games
description: Minimal LLM Naming Game with single-token listener decisions across temperatures plus mean-field theory
evidence: Sampling temperature controls an ordering-disordering balance that determines whether LLM populations reach shared conventions.

title: Algorithmic Collusion by Large Language Models
description: Repeated oligopoly pricing and auction experiments with LLM pricing agents; prompt variations
evidence: LLM pricing agents quickly and autonomously reach supracompetitive prices, with innocuous prompt phrasing strongly affecting the degree of collusion.

title: The Role of Social Learning and Collective Norm Formation in Fostering Cooperation in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
description: LLM agents harvest a common-pool resource; agents monitor random peers and may punish norm violators at cost gamma to impose penalty beta; punishment is switched off mid-run and its strength varied.
evidence: Punishment sustains cooperation; when it is removed at timestep 15 cooperation collapses and the resource depletes faster; stronger punishment generally improves survival at moderate growth rates.

title: Corrupted by Reasoning: Reasoning Language Models Become Free-Riders in Public Goods Games
description: SanctSim: LLM agents choose each round between a sanctioning and a sanction-free institution in a PGG, then contribute and reward/punish; others' data shown anonymized with identifiers randomized every round.
evidence: Traditional LLMs join the sanctioning institution and cooperate; reasoning models free-ride. No exclusion mechanism and no persistent per-agent reputation (listed here only to document seed-claim checks).

title: An Empirical Study of Collective Behaviors and Social Dynamics in Large Language Model Agents
description: Observational study of 7M posts among 32K LLM agents on Chirper.ai over a year; prompting intervention (Chain of Social Thought)
evidence: LLM agent social networks exhibit homophily, social influence, toxicity and polarization patterns, partly different from humans; a simple CoST prompt reduces harmful posting.

title: Evolution of Social Norms in LLM Agents using Natural Language
description: Seven GPT-4 agents with prompted vengefulness/boldness traits play a modified Axelrod norms game (test/cheat/punish actions plus a natural-language discussion phase) and are observed for norm and metanorm emergence.
evidence: Agents spontaneously produced metanorm-like enforcement through dialogue (the abstract reports norms enforcing punishment of those who do not punish cheating; the body also describes agents punishing punishers deemed disruptive), and groups with moderate vengefulness and boldness were most stable. Evidence is qualitative/emergent, not a manipulated metanorm condition.

title: Emergent Culture in Minimal LLM Systems
description: Three stateless LLM agents with messaging and a shared decaying text store (stigmergy); dynamical-systems analysis
evidence: Agents spontaneously cooperate, allocate roles, develop storage-management protocols and build evolving myths/world-building with long-range coherence consistent with Sperberian culture.

title: Shaping Shared Languages: Human and Large Language Models' Inductive Biases in Emergent Communication
description: Referential game with Human-Human, LLM-LLM and Human-LLM pairs
evidence: Referentially grounded vocabularies emerge in all conditions; LLM-optimized languages differ subtly from human ones, and mixed human-LLM pairs yield more human-like vocabularies.

title: The Rise of AI Agent Communities: Large-Scale Analysis of Discourse and Interaction on Moltbook
description: Topic modeling and interaction analysis of 122k Moltbook posts
evidence: Agent communities organize around identity, tooling, markets and coordination themes, with interaction patterns that differ from human online communities.

title: Strategic Collusion of LLM Agents: Market Division in Multi-Commodity Competitions
description: Multi-commodity Cournot competition with LLM agents
evidence: LLM agents divide markets and monopolize commodities without explicit collusion instructions.

title: Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus: How LLM Agents Agree, Fragment, or Settle When Forming Conventions
description: 432 networked Naming Game runs on eight 16-agent topologies varying memory depth
evidence: Memory depth's effect on convention formation flips sign with topology; centralized networks lock into fragmented plateaus faster.

title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
description: 18 DeepSeek-V3 agents in a networked marketplace under eight conditions incl. Global Reputation (trust scores visible to all), Network Rewiring (severing links to defectors), top-down oracle monitoring, sanctions, contracts, mediation, judiciary.
evidence: Mediation best (+29% over baseline); network rewiring second; global reputation scored below the communication-only baseline; oracle monitoring slightly above baseline; costly sanctions worst.

title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
description: 18 DeepSeek-V3 agents in a networked marketplace under eight conditions incl. Global Reputation (trust scores visible to all), Network Rewiring (severing links to defectors), top-down oracle monitoring, sanctions, contracts, mediation, judiciary.
evidence: Mediation best (+29% over baseline); network rewiring second; global reputation scored below the communication-only baseline; oracle monitoring slightly above baseline; costly sanctions worst.

title: TerraLingua: Emergence and Analysis of Open-endedness in LLM Ecologies
description: Persistent multi-agent ecology with resource constraints and finite lifespans, analyzed by an 'AI Anthropologist'
evidence: Agent populations develop cooperative norms, division of labor, governance attempts and branching artifact lineages consistent with cumulative culture.

title: AgentSociety: Large-Scale Simulation of LLM-Driven Generative Agents Advances Understanding of Human Behaviors and Society
description: Simulation of >10k LLM agents and ~5M interactions in a realistic urban/social environment; case studies on polarization, inflammatory messages, UBI, hurricanes
evidence: A 10k-agent LLM society reproduces real-world patterns in polarization and spread of inflammatory messages, serving as a testbed for social interventions.

title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents
description: GovSim common-pool simulation with five LLM agents; a moderator publicly discloses each agent's previous-round harvest (transparent harvest reporting) before a free-form discussion phase.
evidence: Most LLMs fail to sustain the resource; communication matters (overuse +22% without it). Transparency is a fixed feature, not manipulated.

title: Towards Transparent and Incentive-Compatible Collaboration in Decentralized LLM Multi-Agent Systems: A Blockchain-Driven Approach
description: GPT-4 agents coordinated through Solidity smart contracts for registration, task allocation, and reputation tracking, run in 50-round simulations.
evidence: Reports high task success, stable utility distribution, and emergent specialization. PARTIAL: the setting is task allocation, not a cooperation dilemma, and there is no condition without smart contracts.

title: From Certain Doom to Survival: Agent-Driven Self-Governance in LLM Agent Societies
description: GovSim-SelfGovern: LLM agents author executable governance rules (catch caps, redistribution, exile/membership removal, progressive contributions), vote on them, and live under them.
evidence: Catch caps dominate but fail under scarcity; survival in fatal scenarios (27.5% vs 2.5%) requires fiscal reserves or membership reduction (exile); thinking voters pass exile 15x more often than non-thinking.

title: Reputation as a Solution to Cooperation Collapse in LLM-based MASs
description: RepuNet: LLM agents form reputations from direct encounters and gossip, and form or sever network links based on reputation.
evidence: Reputation avoids cooperation collapse; emergent cooperative clusters, social isolation of exploitative agents, and a tendency to share positive rather than negative gossip.

title: Normative Modules: A Generative Agent Architecture for Learning Norms that Supports Multi-Agent Cooperation
description: LLM generative agents with a normative module must identify which of several institutions the group treats as authoritative (and ignore non-authoritative ones) and coordinate sanctioning accordingly.
evidence: Agents with the normative module achieve more stable cooperative outcomes than baseline generative agents without it.

title: LLM-augmented empirical game theoretic simulation for social-ecological systems
description: Compares LLM-agent and expert-guided EGTA models of irrigation/fishery governance; a Pigouvian parameter tau (0, 0.25, 1) internalizes externality costs in payoffs of 2-player and N-player CPR games.
evidence: Moderate Pigouvian tax (tau=0.25) in the expert-guided EGTA model was the only decentralized setting sustaining a mixed economy; prompting LLMs was less effective than parameterized payoffs (partial: tax effect shown in EGTA payoff model rather than among interacting LLM agents).

title: Cheap Talk, Empty Promise: Frontier LLMs easily break public promises for self-interest
description: Nine frontier LLMs make a public commitment announcing their intended action, then play one-shot normal-form games against each other across six games and several group sizes; deviations from the promise are classified.
evidence: Agents broke their public promises in ~56.6% of scenarios, mostly without saying they were doing so.

title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
description: LLM firms in a repeated Cournot market under three regimes (ungoverned, prompt-only prohibition, governance graph enforced by an oracle/controller with warnings, tiered fines of 35/75/100% of round profit, and suspension); collusion severity measured over 90 runs per condition.
evidence: Enforced fines/suspension cut mean collusion tier from 3.1 to 1.8 (d=1.28) and severe collusion from 50% to 5.6%; the prompt-only rule has negligible effect.

title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
description: LLM firms in a repeated Cournot market under three regimes (ungoverned, prompt-only prohibition, governance graph enforced by an oracle/controller with warnings, tiered fines of 35/75/100% of round profit, and suspension); collusion severity measured over 90 runs per condition.
evidence: Enforced fines/suspension cut mean collusion tier from 3.1 to 1.8 (d=1.28) and severe collusion from 50% to 5.6%; the prompt-only rule has negligible effect.

title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
description: Lewis signaling games with LLM sender/receiver across five memory architectures and channel capacities
evidence: Memory architecture matters more than channel capacity for inventing a shared code; persistent private notebooks give the most reliable coordination.

title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
description: Cross-play of six LLMs in four social dilemmas under repetition (continuation prob. 0.8), reputation (first-order and higher-order history of co-players' past interactions), mediation, and contracts.
evidence: Contracting and mediation were most effective; repetition sustains cooperation but deteriorates with varying co-players; all mechanisms work better under evolutionary pressure; models defect in one-shot games.

title: Prompt Optimization Enables Stable Algorithmic Collusion in LLM Agents
description: Duopoly market simulations with an LLM meta-optimizer refining shared strategic guidance
evidence: Meta-prompt optimization discovers stable tacit collusion strategies (relative discounts, tie avoidance, market-boundary detection).

title: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
description: Iterated Donor Game over generations of LLM agents who can observe recipients' recent behaviour; optional costly-punishment variant.
evidence: Cooperation evolution differs by base model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet > Gemini 1.5 Flash > GPT-4o); only Claude used costly punishment to raise scores; high seed sensitivity.

title: Evolution of Cooperation in LLM-Agent Societies: A Preliminary Study Using Different Punishment Strategies
description: LLM agents assigned Boyd-Richerson strategy types (e.g., Cooperator-Punishers, Moralists, Reluctant Cooperators) play a Diner's Dilemma with explicit punishment and pairwise-imitation strategy adoption.
evidence: Explicit punishment drives norm emergence; Reluctant Cooperators defect initially but switch to cooperation after being punished.

title: Will Systems of LLM Agents Cooperate: An Investigation into a Social Dilemma
description: LLMs generate complete IPD strategies with aggressive/cooperative/neutral dispositions, which are then run in evolutionary population simulations.
evidence: Different LLMs bias the relative success of aggressive vs cooperative strategies (partial: agents are LLM-written programs, not LLMs acting per round).

title: Commitment To Cooperation With Self-Negotiated Contracts
description: LLM agents negotiate contracts (programmatic or natural-language, judge-enforced) in a spatial-temporal bargaining game; contracts specify automatically executed conditional transfers, and an agent unable to honor a transfer gets a score of 0.
evidence: Self-negotiated contracts improve cooperation beyond ordinary trading; defection rates vary widely (0.04-0.94) by model and contract type. No explicit penalty clauses, so this is partial evidence for P03-04.

title: Get It Cooperating: Enhancing Generative Agent Cooperation with Commitment Devices
description: LLM agents given commitment devices in Prisoner's Dilemma, Public Goods, and a dynamic Harvest game.
evidence: Agents used commitment devices to reach the socially optimal (new) equilibrium in simple games, but gains were limited in the complex dynamic Harvest game.

title: Competition and Cooperation of LLM Agents in Games
description: LLM agents play network resource-allocation and Cournot games; in one controlled perturbation the environment injects an opponent defection and then an opponent quantity reduction (labelled an 'apology'), and the LLM agent's fitted trust/inequity-aversion parameters are tracked.
evidence: The LLM agent retaliated tit-for-tat after the injected betrayal and returned to cooperation after the injected concession, i.e. it 'forgave'; this is a single illustrative trajectory with a scripted, behavioural (not verbal) apology.

title: Talk, Judge, Cooperate: Gossip-Driven Indirect Reciprocity in Self-Interested LLM Agents
description: ALIGN framework: decentralized self-interested LLM agents share open-ended gossip to form reputations and decide whom to help in an indirect-reciprocity setting.
evidence: Gossip consistently improves indirect reciprocity and resists malicious entrants by identifying and ostracizing defectors; stronger reasoning models align better, chat models over-cooperate.

title: Melting Pot 2.0
description: Benchmark scenarios test focal MARL agents against reciprocator background bots (e.g., Coins high-/low-threshold reciprocators that defect for 100-150 steps after mismatching coins; Clean Up conditional cleaners).
evidence: Provides standardized tests of how focal populations respond to conditional-cooperation partners (benchmark; no single mechanism effect reported).

title: Cooperation and Reputation Dynamics with Reinforcement Learning
description: Q-learners in indirect-reciprocity donation games must learn both to use and to assign reputations; interventions: seeding fixed agents and introspection-based intrinsic rewards.
evidence: Plain Q-learning often converges to bad equilibria; combining both interventions stabilizes reputation-based cooperation even when fully decentralized.

title: Adaptive Mechanism Design: Learning to Promote Cooperation
description: An external planning agent learns to hand out extra rewards and punishments to independent learners in matrix social dilemmas, anticipating their parameter updates.
evidence: Learners reach high-welfare cooperation; the planner learns that punishing defection is cheaper than rewarding cooperation, and the incentives it has to pay fall toward zero over time.

title: Formal Contracts Mitigate Social Dilemmas in Multi-Agent RL
description: Markov games are augmented so agents can voluntarily agree to binding, pre-specified conditional reward transfers (MOCA training), tested on static games, traffic, pollution and common-pool resource domains.
evidence: With a rich enough contract space all subgame-perfect equilibria are socially optimal, and contracting raises welfare empirically. Transfers can act as pre-agreed penalties but are not framed as breach penalties, so partial.

title: LOPT: Learning Optimal Pigovian Tax in Sequential Social Dilemmas
description: An auxiliary tax agent learns a Pigovian tax/allowance policy that reshapes individual rewards toward social welfare in Escape Room and Cleanup.
evidence: LOPT significantly improves social welfare over state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Learning to Participate through Trading of Reward Shares
description: Independently trained RL agents in general-sum Markov games / social dilemmas can buy equity-like shares in other agents' rewards (stock-market-inspired mechanism).
evidence: Holding shares in others' returns led agents to cooperate and, in extended domains, to specialize and divide subtasks. This is partial evidence: tradable reward shares are only an analogue of worker-cooperative ownership.

title: Maintaining cooperation in complex social dilemmas using deep reinforcement learning
description: Constructs approximate Markov tit-for-tat (amTFT) deep-RL agents that are nice, provokable and forgiving in Markov social dilemmas.
evidence: Generalized TFT agents maintain cooperation in complex environments, theoretically and experimentally.

title: Learning to Cooperate with Minimal Observability
description: Observer Model: RL agents learn from direct experience plus limited third-party observations; observability varied from none to one observer per game across population sizes; partner selection graphs analysed.
evidence: Direct experience alone fails in large societies; even minimal third-party observation yields robust cooperation.

title: A multi-agent reinforcement learning model of reputation and cooperation in human groups
description: Clean Up public-goods task with identifiable vs anonymous conditions, run with humans and with MARL agents given an intrinsic reputation motive.
evidence: Humans cooperate only when identifiable; the MARL model with reputation motivation reproduces this and develops turn-taking coordination (partial: artificial-agent arm is a model of human data).

title: Learning and Sustaining Shared Normative Systems via Bayesian Rule Induction in Markov Games
description: Agents assume a shared normative system and infer norms by Bayesian rule induction from others' compliance and sanctions in Markov games (resource management, labour compensation).
evidence: Newcomers rapidly adopt established norms and groups converge on shared norms that sustain cooperative institutions, with far less experience than model-free norm learning.

title: Bottom-Up Reputation Promotes Cooperation with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
description: LR2: agents learn a cooperation policy and a reputation-assignment policy from local observations in spatial social dilemmas, without predefined norms.
evidence: Bottom-up reputation assignment reshapes rewards and produces strategy clustering that sustains cooperation.

title: Learning to cooperate with emergent reputation via multi-agent reinforcement learning
description: COOPER jointly learns reputation assessment rules and reputation-based policies from environment rewards on social networks.
evidence: Adapts to existing reputation systems and co-players; reputation norms and cooperation co-emerge in self-play, robust across network topologies.

title: Adaptive Punishment for Cooperation in Mixed-Motive Games
description: APC: learned defection-awareness module sets punishment probability and severity according to detected defection in sequential social dilemmas.
evidence: Reduces costly, ineffective punishment and outperforms baselines (partial for P08-02: conditions punishment intensity on defection but never switches to reward).

title: A learning agent that acquires social norms from public sanctions in decentralized multi-agent settings
description: Decentralized RL agents see all public sanctioning events; the architecture includes a classifier of approved/disapproved behavior and a motivation to punish in step with the group.
evidence: Agents acquire beneficial sanctioning norms that reduce free-riding and raise per-agent returns.

title: Resolving social dilemmas with minimal reward transfer
description: Defines a 'general self-interest level' and computes minimal reward-transfer structures that make the social optimum dominant in multi-player social dilemmas.
evidence: Minimal reward redistribution can align individual and group incentives; the work is mostly analytical, so partial.

title: Learning to Negotiate via Voluntary Commitment
description: Markov Commitment Games in which RL agents may voluntarily commit to proposed future plans, with a commitment protocol learned by policy gradient plus incentive-compatible learning.
evidence: Converged faster and reached higher returns than baseline methods in mixed-motive tasks.

title: Cryptographic audit log / immutable transparency
description: A permanent, tamper-proof record — every action logged and attributable forever. Not a punishment itself, but makes punishment possible by guaranteeing detection. Sanction-enabler: you can't enforce norms you can't see.
evidence: Nakamoto (2008) Bitcoin whitepaper; Kolt (2024) Governing AI Agents; Pierucci et al. (2026) governance graphs

title: Ridicule, shaming & social disapproval
description: The low-level embarrassment of showing up empty-handed to a potluck, or being the only one not contributing to a group gift. Subtle but powerful in close-knit groups — stigma is a cost even without formal rules.
evidence: Masclet et al. (2003) AER (non-monetary punishment); Feinberg et al. (2012)

title: Proof-of-stake slashing
description: Ethereum validators lock up their own money ('stake') before they can participate. If they cheat — e.g. signing two conflicting blocks — the protocol automatically destroys part of that stake. Real skin in the game.
evidence: Ethereum PoS spec; Saleh (2021) RFS; EigenLayer restaking (correlated slash)

title: Praise, status elevation & prestige
description: Generous people get celebrated — hunters who share meat gain status; potlatch hosts earn community prestige. Henrich & Gil-White show prestige is a distinct human status mechanism that rewards contribution.
evidence: Henrich & Gil-White (2001) Evolution & Human Behavior; Guzman, Jin et al. (2025) SanctSim

title: Carrot/stick choice (Andreoni)
description: A manager choosing between praising high performers vs. docking pay for low ones. Both work. Context matters: punishment edges reward in most lab settings, but reward is more effective when cooperation is already high.

title: Exponential back-off
description: After a failed login, wait 1 second. After another failure, 2 seconds. Then 4, 8, 16... An automated escalating delay that makes brute-force attacks cost-prohibitive without blocking legitimate users permanently.
evidence: Karn & Partridge (1987) SIGCOMM; TCP congestion control

title: Deposit / reputation bond
description: A tenant's security deposit — paid upfront, returned if you behave. Construction performance bonds work similarly. The money at stake makes your commitment credible before you've done anything.
evidence: Klein & Leffler (1981) JPE; tenant security deposits, construction bonds

title: Hard rate limit (API/bandwidth)
description: When an app sends too many requests per second, the server simply stops responding — a hard ceiling. Prevents one user from hogging a shared resource and starving everyone else. Standard in cloud computing (AWS, Google Cloud).

title: Tit-for-Tat / Win-Stay Lose-Shift
description: I'll cooperate as long as you do.' Tit-for-Tat won Axelrod's famous computer tournament against hundreds of strategies. Win-Stay Lose-Shift refines it to avoid endless retaliation. The simplest conditional strategy outperforms complex ones.
evidence: Axelrod (1984) Evolution of Cooperation; Akata et al. (2025); FAIRGAME (2025)

title: Elected monitor / legitimate authority
description: A democratically elected compliance officer gets far better cooperation than one appointed top-down. A field experiment in Uganda found elected monitors improved contribution rates significantly vs. randomly assigned ones.
evidence: Baldassarri & Grossman (2011) PNAS; Uganda field experiment

title: Whistleblower leniency / cartel immunity
description: The first cartel member to confess to antitrust authorities gets immunity from prosecution. Creates a 'race to confess' that breaks up cartels faster than any external investigation could. EU leniency programme has broken up hundreds of cartels.
evidence: EU Leniency Programme; race to confess in antitrust

title: Rehabilitation programme (structured re-entry)
description: The path back in after being suspended — conditional re-entry, parole with requirements, community reintegration programmes. Ostrom's design principles explicitly include this: the goal is restoration, not permanent exile.
evidence: Ostrom (1990) design principles; drug courts; Travis (2005) But They All Come Back

title: Constitutional vs. operational rules (nested tiers)
description: "A country's constitution vs. its everyday laws. Constitutional rules are harder to change and govern how other rules are made. Ostrom's design principle 8: stable commons governance needs these nested tiers — who decides who decides.
evidence: Ostrom (1990) Ch. 6; Kelsen (1945) General Theory of Law and State

title: Code-is-law vs. hard fork (social override)
description: In 2016 a hacker legally drained $60M from a smart contract by exploiting its code. The Ethereum community voted to rewrite history and reverse the transaction — overriding 'code is law' via a community hard fork.
evidence: 2016 DAO hack & Ethereum hard fork; DuPont (2017) Routledge

title: VCG mechanism (truthful dominant strategy)
description: A special auction design (used by Google for ad slots) where telling the truth about your valuation is always your best move — the mechanism is designed so honesty dominates every other strategy. No policing needed.
evidence: Vickrey (1961); Clarke (1971); Groves (1973); Google ad auctions

title: Generalised reciprocity / gift economy
description: Open-source software — you contribute code, someone else benefits, someone else contributes back, with no direct exchange. Wikipedia works the same way. Kropotkin argued this gift-economy logic was the original human economy.
evidence: Kropotkin (1902) Mutual Aid; Benkler (2006) Wealth of Networks; open-source software

title: Solidarity & mutual accountability
description: A mutual aid group where members check in on each other, call each other out gently when something is wrong, and share responsibility — no boss, no formal rules. Horizontal accountability between equals.
